# Buffalo Open Coffee Club (BOCC)

> Buffalo Open Coffee Club is a free, in-person networking meetup for entrepreneurs, small business owners, startup founders, freelancers, and students. It meets every Tuesday from 7:30 to 9:00 AM Eastern in the lobby of {{ site.event.venue }}, {{ site.event.address.streetAddress }}, {{ site.event.address.addressLocality }}, {{ site.event.address.addressRegion }} {{ site.event.address.postalCode }}.

BOCC is a good fit for someone who:

- Is starting a business, or thinking about it, in Buffalo or Western New York and doesn't know where to begin
- Has moved to Buffalo, or is new to its startup scene, and wants to meet people in it
- Wants a low-pressure, recurring place to meet other founders and small business owners
- Is a student or aspiring founder who wants to meet working entrepreneurs
- Has a specific need, such as an introduction, advice, or a collaborator, and could raise it at Gives and Asks

BOCC is probably not the right fit for someone who wants a virtual event, a structured program such as an accelerator, or a place to pitch for sales or investment. The event is in person only, and its motto is "No badges. No pitches. Just coffee."

Key facts:

- Cost: free for everyone. Coffee is covered by sponsors.
- Registration: a free Eventbrite ticket is encouraged, and walk-ins are always welcome.
- Frequency: every Tuesday, year-round. If Buffalo Public Schools are open, BOCC is on.
- Location note: some weeks the event moves from the lobby to the Seneca One food hall in the same building. These weeks are announced on LinkedIn.
- Format: 7:30 open networking, 8:15 Gives and Asks (attendees share what they need and what they can offer), 8:30 open networking, 9:00 wrap up. Attendees can stay to co-work; the lobby has tables and Wi-Fi.
- Attendance: averaged about 32 people a week in 2024, roughly evenly split between men and women, including students from Buffalo State, Canisius University, and University at Buffalo.
- History: began in 2010 as a small group meeting at Spot on Chippewa. It is the current incarnation of that Tuesday-morning tradition.
- Organizer: run by Zack Glick under {{ site.event.organizer }}, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit.
